tasks.title: Extract post-iteration logic from run.ts into settleTask (src/settle.ts)
tasks.description:
Extract the post-iteration logic of `cairn run` into a new, independently tested module `src/settle.ts`. This is a PURE EXTRACTION: the behavior of `cairn run` must not change, and `test/commands/run.test.ts` must stay green without weakening any assertion.

CONTEXT: Round 15 adds a second way to run a round (`/cairn-run`, an interactive session that drives new `cairn round next` / `cairn round settle` CLI commands). Both modes must share ONE tested implementation of the post-iteration logic. This task creates that shared function; later tasks (93, 94, 95, 97) extend it with persisted counters, an incomplete guard, verdict JSON and a review phase.

WHAT TO MOVE: in `src/commands/run.ts` inside `runRun`, steps k (validateTaskTests), k2 (consecutive-revert guard, REVERT_BLOCK_THRESHOLD = 2), k3 (re-read the task status from tasks.json) and k4 (same-task stall guard, STALL_BLOCK_THRESHOLD = 3) — currently roughly lines 665-740. Move both threshold constants (with their doc comments) and `summarizeFailure` into `src/settle.ts` and export what run.ts needs.

DESIGN:
- Export an async `settleTask(input, deps)`. Input: task, selectedStatus (the status snapshot at selection time — keep it for now; task 94 removes it), tasksFilePath, dataDir, projectRoot, iteration, iterationLogPath. Deps are injected with the same shapes as RunRunDeps: validateTaskTests, readTasksFile, blockTask, appendFileSync, log, plus a counters object.
- Counters live behind an interface, e.g. `GuardCounters { get(taskId, kind): number; set(taskId, kind, n): void; clear(taskId, kind): void }` with kind 'reverts' | 'stalls', plus an exported in-memory implementation backed by Maps. runRun creates one in-memory instance per run, preserving today's per-run semantics (task 93 makes them persistent).
- Return a result object carrying at least: the validation result, updatedTaskStatus ('unknown' when tasks.json is unreadable), whether a guard blocked the task (so runRun can keep maintaining `blockedByGuard`), and a corruption flag (repaired/restored) so runRun keeps counting corruptionEvents.
- runRun calls settleTask and then continues with step l (post-task review) and step m (archive) exactly as today, in the same order.

TESTS: create `test/settle.test.ts` with fake deps (no real processes) covering: passed validation resets reverts; failed validation increments reverts and blocks at 2 with the existing note text; a stall increments only when the task was selected pending and is still pending, and blocks at 3; any other observed status resets stalls; an unreadable tasks file leaves both guards neutral.

tasks.title: Run-state store (src/run-state.ts)
tasks.description:
Create `src/run-state.ts`: a small, locked, atomic store for round runtime state, persisted in a gitignored temp file inside the data dir.

CONTEXT: guard counters (reverts, stalls, and a new 'incompletes') are currently in-memory Maps inside runRun (src/commands/run.ts). Under the new `/cairn-run` mode the loop driver is a model that can be compacted, resumed or restarted, so counters and per-task attempt data must live on disk. Later tasks (93+) wire this store in; this task only builds and tests it.

FILE: path via `tempFilePath(dataDir, 'run_state.json')` (src/utils.ts), i.e. `.cairn_run_state.json`. Callers pass an already-resolved dataDir (from findDataDir) — never rebuild the path from BRAND.dataDir (CLAUDE.md convention: BRAND constants are for creating paths, discovery for resolving them).

SHAPE (export the types RunState, AttemptRecord, AttemptPhase):
{ iteration: number, attempts: { [taskId: string]: { beforeSha: string | null, iteration: number, reverts: number, stalls: number, incompletes: number, phase: 'executing' | 'awaiting-review' } } }

API (suggested names):
- `readRunState(dataDir): RunState` — missing file returns `{ iteration: 0, attempts: {} }`; an unparseable file is treated as empty and does not throw (runtime state is disposable).
- `updateRunState(dataDir, fn: (state) => T): T` — acquire `acquireLock(<statePath>.lock)` from src/file-lock.ts, read, apply fn (mutating the state), write atomically (unique temp file + rename, mirroring writeTasksFile in src/tasks-file.ts), and in a finally block close the fd and unlink the lock. Returns fn's result. The lock must be released when fn throws.
- Convenience helpers such as `getAttempt(dataDir, taskId)` and `clearAttempt(dataDir, taskId)`.

LOCKING RULES — document these in the module header comment; later tasks rely on them:
- Critical sections must be SHORT. acquireLock treats a lock older than 60s as stale and breaks it, while test validation can run 120s per command. Never hold the run-state lock across test validation, agent execution or health checks; do read-modify-write in short updateRunState calls.
- acquireLock is not reentrant. Lock ordering: the run-state lock may be taken before the tasks.json lock (mutateTasksFile takes `tasks.json.lock` internally), never the reverse — never call updateRunState from inside a mutateTasksFile callback.

GITIGNORE (required): add `'run_state.json'` and `'run_state.json.lock'` to `TEMP_IGNORE_SUFFIXES` in src/commands/init.ts, and update the expected ignore-block lines asserted in test/commands/init.test.ts (around lines 70-100).

TESTS: `test/run-state.test.ts`, all in temp dirs (fs.mkdtempSync): empty default; write/read round-trip; updateRunState returns fn's value; a corrupt file is tolerated; the lock file is gone after an update; the lock is released when fn throws.

tasks.title: Persist guard counters in run state; cairn task set-status clears the attempt record
tasks.description:
Make settleTask's guard counters persistent via the run-state store, so counters survive process restarts and separate settle invocations.

CONTEXT: task 91 extracted `settleTask` into src/settle.ts with an injected in-memory GuardCounters (reverts, stalls). Task 92 added src/run-state.ts (`.cairn_run_state.json`: `{ iteration, attempts: { [taskId]: { beforeSha, iteration, reverts, stalls, incompletes, phase } } }`, with readRunState / updateRunState / clearAttempt). Counters are runtime state, not task data — do NOT add fields to the Task type or src/tasks-schema.json.

CHANGES:
1. Run-state-backed counters: implement GuardCounters over the attempt record (reverts/stalls stored in `attempts[id]`). settleTask reads and writes counters through short updateRunState calls. runRun stops using the in-memory implementation (keep it only if tests still need it).
2. Attempt record at pick time in `cairn run` (src/commands/run.ts): after selecting a task and before spawning the agent, create the attempt record if none exists: `{ beforeSha: captureGitSha(projectRoot), iteration, reverts: 0, stalls: 0, incompletes: 0, phase: 'executing' }`. If a record already exists (a re-pick of the same task), KEEP its original beforeSha so the eventual review covers every attempt, and update its iteration. runRun then passes the recorded beforeSha to the review step instead of a freshly captured one.
3. Record lifecycle for now: clear the record when a guard blocks the task (so a human unblocking gets fresh attempts, as the existing comments intend) and when a task observed complete has gone through runRun's review/archive steps. Tasks 95 and 97 formalize the lifecycle; keep this simple and tested.
4. `cairn task set-status <id> <status>` (taskSetStatus in src/commands/task.ts) clears the task's attempt record AFTER mutateTasksFile returns successfully — never inside its callback (lock ordering). TaskSetStatusOpts already has an optional dataDir; when absent, skip clearing. A failure to clear must not fail the command: write a warning to stderr and still return 0.
5. Rewrite the comment at run.ts ~489 ('In-memory and per-run on purpose: a livelock only matters inside a single run...'): counters are now runtime state in the gitignored run-state file; restarting `cairn run` no longer resets them; `cairn task set-status` is the reset; they are still not a Task field. Fix the matching comment on consecutiveStalls.

LOCKING: never hold the run-state lock across validateTaskTests (a 120s test run outlives acquireLock's 60s stale-lock threshold), and never take it inside a mutateTasksFile callback.

TESTS: test/settle.test.ts — counters survive two separate settleTask calls against the same temp data dir (e.g. two failed validations across two calls block the task). test/commands/task.test.ts — set-status clears the record; missing dataDir or a clear failure does not fail the command. test/commands/run.test.ts — attempt record created at pick with beforeSha, kept on re-pick; adapt existing run tests to the new dependency (inject run-state access through deps or use a temp dataDir) without weakening them.

tasks.title: Incomplete guard (in-progress at settle, limit 3) and stall-note rewording
tasks.description:
Close the in-progress livelock gap and reword the stall-guard note, in src/settle.ts.

CONTEXT: settleTask (src/settle.ts, tasks 91 and 93) runs after an agent iteration, with counters persisted in the run-state attempt record (`.cairn_run_state.json` via src/run-state.ts: reverts, stalls, incompletes). Today a task the agent leaves 'in-progress' every iteration (timeout, giving up) is re-picked until maxIterations runs out: selectNextTask returns in-progress tasks first, the revert guard only counts failed validations of COMPLETE tasks, and the stall guard only counts PENDING tasks and resets when it sees in-progress.

CHANGES:
1. Incomplete guard: when the task's status at settle time is 'in-progress' and it was NOT reverted by a failed validation in this same settle, increment `incompletes`. A failed validation counts ONLY as a revert, never as an incomplete. Add an exported INCOMPLETE_BLOCK_THRESHOLD = 3 with a doc comment in the style of the existing constants: fixed, not configurable; 3 rather than 2 because blocking early costs a human unblock while blocking late costs one extra agent session, a large task can legitimately need two sessions, and the third attempt deliberately uses a fresh agent in case the first agent's own context was the problem. At 3: block the task via blockTask with a clear note (e.g. `Blocked by cairn after 3 consecutive iterations that left the task 'in-progress' without completing it.`) and clear the attempt record.
2. Expose the retry mode for the next attempt on settleTask's result as `retryMode`: incompletes 1 → 'continue' (resume the same agent), incompletes 2 → 'fresh', 3 → blocked. A stall (still pending) is always 'fresh'. A failed validation below its threshold → 'continue'. Task 95 turns this into verdict JSON.
3. Stall detection no longer depends on selectedStatus: a task still 'pending' at settle time is a stall. Remove the selectedStatus input from settleTask and from its caller in run.ts (including the `selectedStatus` snapshot variable and its comment).
4. Resets: observing in-progress, complete or blocked resets stalls. Observing in-progress does NOT reset incompletes. A passed validation resets reverts and incompletes.
5. Reword the stall note (it currently blames a permissions.deny rule for 'cairn task' in .claude/settings.local.json). cairn init now strips those rules, and under /cairn-run a stall has other causes. The new note keeps the 'Blocked by cairn after N consecutive iterations in which the agent never moved the task out of pending' phrasing and lists likely causes without asserting one: the agent could not run the cairn CLI (not on PATH, or a permission rule or hook denying it), it crashed or hit its turn limit before starting, or it misread its instructions. Update the STALL_BLOCK_THRESHOLD doc comment and any deps.log message in run.ts that names permissions.deny as the cause.

This intentionally also changes `cairn run` (it shares settleTask): a task left in-progress three times is now blocked there too.

TESTS (test/settle.test.ts, test/commands/run.test.ts): incompletes 1/2/3 progression with retry modes and the block; a failed validation increments only reverts; still-pending is a stall regardless of prior status; the new note does not claim permissions.deny as the cause; update any run.test.ts assertion on the old note or on selectedStatus.

tasks.title: Settle verdict JSON, record-based idempotency, next hints, error types
tasks.description:
Define the settle verdict contract and make settle idempotent based on the attempt record.

CONTEXT: settleTask (src/settle.ts) validates, applies guards and persists counters in the run-state attempt record (src/run-state.ts; tasks 91/93, and task 94 adds `retryMode` and the incomplete guard — if 94 has landed, build on its retryMode). A new CLI `cairn round settle <id>` (wired in task 99) will be called by an interactive run agent that may be compacted or resumed, so every call must be safe to repeat and every output must tell the caller what to do next.

CHANGES in src/settle.ts:
1. Exported Verdict union (the CLI will print it as JSON):
- `{ verdict: 'retry', taskId, mode: 'continue' | 'fresh', reason, failure?, next }` — `failure` gets the last ~40 lines of test output from task 96; keep it optional.
- `{ verdict: 'blocked', taskId, reason, next }` — a guard block, or the agent itself set status 'blocked' (reason taken from the task's notes; clear the record).
- `{ verdict: 'done', taskId, reason?, next }` — task 97 adds reasons such as 'review-disabled' | 'no-commits' | 'no-before-sha' | 'reviewed'.
- `{ verdict: 'already-settled', taskId, next }`.
(Task 97 adds a `review` verdict.) Every verdict has `next`, a short imperative hint for the driver: 'Run: cairn round next' for done/blocked/already-settled; for retry/continue 'Resume the same task agent with SendMessage, then run: cairn round settle <id>' (and say: if that agent's id is lost, launch a fresh cairn-task-agent instead); for retry/fresh 'Launch a fresh cairn-task-agent with the same prompt file, then run: cairn round settle <id>'.
2. Retry mode mapping: stall → fresh; incompletes 1 → continue, 2 → fresh; failed validation below the revert threshold → continue.
3. Idempotency keyed on the ATTEMPT RECORD, not on archived status (task 97 makes settle archive before its review gate, so a status-based check would swallow later calls):
- No record, task id absent from tasks.json but present in tasks.completed.json → `already-settled`, no side effects.
- No record, task present in tasks.json → create the record lazily (beforeSha null for now — task 97 adds a commit-message fallback; iteration from run state) and proceed normally.
- Unknown id (in neither file) → throw a typed `SettleError`.
4. Record lifecycle: clear the record on 'done' and on every block; keep it on 'retry'.
5. settleTask returns the verdict alongside the fields runRun already uses; keep runRun working — it ignores retry modes and simply continues its loop.
6. Append one line per settle to the iterations log (`tempFilePath(dataDir, 'iterations.log')`), e.g. `Settle #<id>: <verdict> (<reason>)`.

EXIT-CODE CONTRACT (implement the error types here; the CLI in task 99 maps them): exit 0 for every verdict, including blocked and already-settled; non-zero only when settle itself cannot run — unreadable tasks.json after repair/recovery (TasksFileError), lock timeout (FileLockError), unknown task id (SettleError).

TESTS (test/settle.test.ts): each verdict shape including `next`; a second call after done → already-settled; missing record with the task present → record created; unknown id throws SettleError; agent-set blocked → blocked verdict with the notes as reason and the record cleared.

tasks.title: Test validation writes a per-task log and returns a summary plus failure tail
tasks.description:
Make test validation write full output to a per-task log file and return a compact summary plus a failure tail.

CONTEXT: validateTaskTests (src/test-validator.ts) runs a task's declared `tests` after the agent marks it complete; a real failure reverts the task to in-progress. Round 15 changes who sees test output: the run agent should only get a short failure tail, and the post-task reviewer only a summary plus the log path (the reviewer will no longer re-run tests). settleTask in src/settle.ts calls validateTaskTests.

CHANGES:
1. Log file: write each command's full combined stdout+stderr, with a header per command (command, cwd, exit code, duration), to `tempFilePath(dataDir, 'task_<id>_tests.log')` — i.e. `.cairn_task_<id>_tests.log`. dataDir is path.dirname(tasksFilePath), as today. Overwrite on each validation run. A failure to write the log must not change the validation outcome. Do not add this log to run.ts's end-of-loop temp-file cleanup — the reviewer reads it later.
2. Extend ValidationResult, keeping the existing `status` and `message` fields and semantics (`message` still carries the 200-character output slice used in the task note):
- `logPath?: string`
- `summary?: Array<{ command: string, status: 'passed' | 'failed' | 'error' | 'skipped', durationMs: number, counts?: { pass?: number, fail?: number, skip?: number } }>` — counts parsed when recognizable (bun test prints lines like ' 12 pass' and ' 0 fail'); be lenient and leave counts undefined when not parseable.
- `failureTail?: string` — the last ~40 lines of the failing command's output, for failed and error results.
3. Export `formatTestSummary(result): string`, producing a few lines suitable for a reviewer prompt (per command: command, status, counts, duration; then the log path). A skipped validation should say so.
4. settleTask: put failureTail into the retry verdict's `failure` field if the Verdict type exists (task 95); otherwise expose it on the settle result.

tasks.title: Review phase in settle: archive then review gate, awaiting-review, --reviewed, beforeSha fallback
tasks.description:
Add the review phase to settle, reorder to archive-then-review, and make repeated calls safe.

CONTEXT: settleTask (src/settle.ts) validates tests, applies guards with counters in the run-state attempt record (src/run-state.ts; phase is 'executing' | 'awaiting-review') and returns verdicts (task 95: retry / blocked / done / already-settled, each with a `next` hint). Today `cairn run` reviews BEFORE archiving (run.ts step l, then m). The new order is validate → archive → review gate. Because archiving happens before the review, idempotency is keyed on the attempt record's phase.

CHANGES in src/settle.ts:
1. For a task that is complete after validation (skipped or passed; 'error' continues with a logged warning): archive via archiveCompletedTasks (src/task-archiver.ts), then apply the review gate with the same conditions as runPostTaskReview (src/post-task-reviewer.ts): config.review?.postTask is enabled; beforeSha is non-null; HEAD differs from beforeSha. If the gate does not pass: clear the record and return `done` with reason 'review-disabled' | 'no-before-sha' | 'no-commits'.
2. If the gate passes: set the record's phase to 'awaiting-review', write the reviewer prompt file, and return `{ verdict: 'review', taskId, reviewPromptFile, next }`, where next says: launch the post-task-reviewer agent with the prompt 'Read <reviewPromptFile> and follow it', then run `cairn round settle <id> --reviewed`.
3. Reviewer prompt file: `tempFilePath(dataDir, 'task_<id>_review_prompt.md')` — i.e. `.cairn_task_<id>_review_prompt.md`. Put the writer in an exported function (e.g. `writeReviewPromptFile`). Its content for now: buildPostTaskReviewUserPrompt with getGitDiff(projectRoot, beforeSha) output and the round review file path computed exactly as spawnPostTaskReviewer does (getRound from src/task-counter.ts + the resolved `<dataDir>/reviews` dir). Task 101 will switch it to a diff-range + test-summary variant. The task object comes from tasks.completed.json, since it has been archived.
4. Idempotency:
- With `reviewed: true` (CLI `--reviewed`): requires a record in phase 'awaiting-review' → clear the record and return `done` with reason 'reviewed'. With no such record: if the task is archived → `already-settled`; otherwise throw SettleError.
- Without `reviewed` while the record is 'awaiting-review' → return `review` again with no other side effects (no re-validation, no re-archive); rewrite the prompt file only if it is missing.
5. beforeSha resolution: an explicit `beforeSha` option (CLI `--before-sha`) overrides the record. When the record is created lazily (none existed), derive beforeSha from git history instead of null: find the oldest commit whose message contains `Task #<id>:` (e.g. `git log --reverse --format=%H --fixed-strings --grep='Task #<id>:'`) and use its parent (`<sha>^`, resolved with git rev-parse); if none is found, null. Inject git access via deps for tests.
6. `cairn run` (src/commands/run.ts): adopt the new order via settleTask. On a `review` verdict, runRun runs the headless reviewer (runPostTaskReview / spawnPostTaskReviewer, as today), then settles again with reviewed: true. `cairn run` keeps its inline prompts — do not move it to prompt files. Update test/commands/run.test.ts for archive-before-review and keep it green.

GITIGNORE (required): add `'task_*_prompt.md'` to `TEMP_IGNORE_SUFFIXES` in src/commands/init.ts and update the ignore-block assertions in test/commands/init.test.ts. This ONE pattern intentionally covers BOTH the reviewer prompt file added here (`.cairn_task_<id>_review_prompt.md`) AND the task-agent prompt file (`.cairn_task_<id>_prompt.md`) that task 98 adds; task 98 reuses this pattern and does not add another. Mention that in a comment next to the suffix.

TESTS (test/settle.test.ts): complete + passed with review enabled → archived, `review` verdict, record awaiting-review; a repeat call → `review` again with no second archive; `reviewed` → done and record cleared; review disabled / no commits / null sha → done with the matching reason; commit-message fallback resolves the parent sha; `beforeSha` override. test/commands/run.test.ts: archive happens before review, and review is followed by a reviewed settle.

tasks.title: roundNext(): pending review first, select, health check, attempt record, prompt file
tasks.description:
Implement `roundNext()` in a new src/commands/round.ts — the pick step of `/cairn-run`. Do NOT register a CLI command in src/index.ts; task 99 does that.

CONTEXT: /cairn-run is an interactive run agent that loops: `cairn round next` → launch a `cairn-task-agent` subagent with 'Read <promptFile> and follow it' → `cairn round settle <id>`. All deterministic logic lives in the CLI; the run agent never reads tasks.json. Available pieces: selectNextTask / loadCompletedIds / buildIterationPrompt (src/task-selector.ts), runHealthCheck (src/health-check.ts), readTasksFile (src/tasks-file.ts), captureGitSha (src/post-task-reviewer.ts), run state (src/run-state.ts: an iteration counter plus attempts with phase 'executing' | 'awaiting-review'), settle's exported review prompt writer (src/settle.ts, task 97), and buildSystemPrompt with `mode: 'subagent'` (src/commands/run.ts, task 100).

roundNext({ projectRoot, dataDir, config, agents }, deps) returns a JSON-serializable object:
1. If any attempt record is in phase 'awaiting-review', return that review first: `{ verdict: 'review', taskId, reviewPromptFile, next }`, rewriting the prompt file if it is missing (reuse task 97's writer). Reviews must not be lost to a crash.
2. Read tasks.json (readTasksFile with repair/recovery) and call selectNextTask. If nothing is ready: `{ verdict: 'round-done', blocked: <count of blocked tasks>, next }` with next telling the driver to send a notification and stop.
3. Run the health check (config.healthCheck, projectRoot). A failure's output is prepended to the iteration prompt exactly as runRun does.
4. Attempt record: create it with beforeSha = HEAD ONLY if none exists; on a re-pick keep the original beforeSha so the review covers every attempt.
5. Increment `iteration` in run state (a short updateRunState call) and store it on the record; it feeds `cairn task start --iteration`.
6. Write the prompt file: the system prompt (buildSystemPrompt in subagent mode) followed by a horizontal-rule separator line and the iteration prompt (buildIterationPrompt; pass sensible values for maxIterations and totalRemaining, and test them), to `tempFilePath(dataDir, 'task_<id>_prompt.md')` — i.e. `.cairn_task_<id>_prompt.md`.
7. Return `{ verdict: 'task', taskId, title, iteration, model, promptFile, next }`, where next says: launch the Agent tool with subagent_type 'cairn-task-agent', model <model>, prompt 'Read <promptFile> and follow it', then run `cairn round settle <id>`.

MODEL: extract runRun's model resolution (run.ts ~564: task.model ?? 'opus', using the specialist agent's model when task.agent is set and task.model is not) into an exported shared helper (e.g. `resolveTaskModel(task, agents)`), used by both runRun and roundNext.

tasks.description:
Implement `cairn hook pre-tool-use`: a Claude Code PreToolUse hook (JSON on stdin) that mechanically contains subagents under /cairn-run.

CONTEXT: under /cairn-run, subagents follow the interactive session's permission mode (recommended: bypassPermissions), so per-agent --allowedTools scoping doesn't apply and agent frontmatter can't express path scopes. Probe results from a throwaway repo with interactive `claude --dangerously-skip-permissions`:
- Main-session tool calls have NO `agent_id` and NO `agent_type` keys (absent, not null). Subagent calls carry `agent_id` plus `agent_type`: 'general-purpose' for the built-in, the agent's frontmatter `name` for custom agents (e.g. 'post-task-reviewer').
- An internal Claude Code helper also fires the hook: a Bash call (`printf 'wait for it'`) with an `agent_id` but NO `agent_type` key. A missing agent_type is normal, not an error.
- Input also includes hook_event_name, permission_mode (e.g. bypassPermissions), tool_name, tool_input, cwd, session_id, transcript_path, tool_use_id.
- Hook denies bind even under bypass mode. Exit 2 shows the agent `PreToolUse:Write hook error: [<script>]: <stderr>`; exit 0 with stdout JSON `{ hookSpecificOutput: { hookEventName: 'PreToolUse', permissionDecision: 'deny', permissionDecisionReason: <reason> } }` shows only the reason. USE THE JSON FORM.
- Any other failure (exit 1, or a missing binary with exit 127) lets the call through SILENTLY.

DECISION FUNCTION (pure, exported; e.g. src/hook-policy.ts or inside src/commands/hook.ts): `decidePreToolUse(input, ctx)` returning `{ decision: 'allow' }` or `{ decision: 'deny', reason }`, where ctx holds the resolved tasksFilePath, reviewsDir and projectRoot.
- Fast path: no `agent_id` → allow immediately (main session, generate-tasks, and every headless `cairn run` agent — the hook is a no-op for them). tool_name not Edit/Write/Bash → allow.
- Rule 1: any subagent (agent_id present, agent_type or not) calling Edit or Write whose tool_input.file_path resolves (relative paths against input.cwd) to the tasks.json path → deny, with a reason pointing to the `cairn task` subcommands.
- Rule 2: only when agent_type === 'post-task-reviewer' exactly: Edit/Write allowed only for paths inside the resolved reviews dir; Bash allowed only when every subcommand (split on &&, ||, ;, |, & and newlines, as buildCommandRules in src/claude-settings.ts documents) starts with one of the prefixes derived from the exported GIT_INSPECTION_RULES (e.g. 'git diff') — derive them from that list, do not duplicate it. Anything else from the reviewer → deny with a reason.
- Everything else → allow (print nothing, exit 0).

CLI: register a `hook` command group with `pre-tool-use` in src/index.ts.
- FAST STARTUP: the hook fires on every Edit/Write/Bash call in every session in the project. index.ts's preAction runs setupProjectContext (loadConfig, discoverAgents, possibly `git rev-parse`) — skip that for the hook command (e.g. check the action command's name in the preAction hook). A malformed cairn.json must be logged, not crash with a stack trace.
- Deny: exit 0 with the hookSpecificOutput JSON on stdout.

CONTEXT: /cairn-run runs a full Cairn round from an interactive Claude Code session (reachable from a phone via Remote Control) instead of headless `cairn run`. The session is the RUN AGENT; all deterministic logic is in the CLI:
- `cairn round next` prints JSON: `{ verdict: 'task', taskId, title, iteration, model, promptFile, next }` | `{ verdict: 'review', taskId, reviewPromptFile, next }` | `{ verdict: 'round-done', blocked, next }`, optionally with `warnings`.
- `cairn round settle <id> [--reviewed]` prints a JSON verdict: `retry` (mode 'continue' | 'fresh', reason, failure tail), `review` (reviewPromptFile), `blocked` (reason), `done`, `already-settled`. Every verdict has a `next` hint. Exit 0 for all verdicts; non-zero means the command itself failed.
- Task agents: subagent_type `cairn-task-agent` (maxTurns 150), return at most 5 lines. Reviewer: subagent_type `post-task-reviewer`, returns one line (PASS or CONCERNS).
Read src/commands/round.ts and src/settle.ts to match the actual JSON fields before writing.

THE COMMAND FILE must instruct the run agent to:
1. Loop: run `cairn round next` and act on the verdict. For `task`: launch the Agent tool with subagent_type 'cairn-task-agent', the model from the JSON, and prompt 'Read <promptFile> and follow it'; remember the returned agent id; then run `cairn round settle <taskId>`.
2. On `review` (from next or settle): launch Agent with subagent_type 'post-task-reviewer' and prompt 'Read <reviewPromptFile> and follow it', then run `cairn round settle <taskId> --reviewed`.
3. On `retry` with mode 'continue': SendMessage to the same task agent id with the reason/failure, asking it to finish, then settle again. If the agent id is unknown (e.g. after compaction or resume), fall back to a fresh cairn-task-agent with the same prompt file. Mode 'fresh': launch a new cairn-task-agent with the same prompt file, then settle.
4. On `blocked`: send a PushNotification (task id + reason) and continue the loop — never pause with AskUserQuestion.
5. On `round-done`: send a PushNotification with a short summary, then stop.
6. On any non-zero exit from a `cairn round` command: send a PushNotification with the stderr line and STOP.
7. Surface `warnings` from next (e.g. hook errors) to the user once.
8. Rules: agents run one at a time, never in parallel and never nested (the task agent must not launch the reviewer); the run agent NEVER reads tasks.json, diffs or test logs itself and never edits tasks.json; always follow each command's `next` hint so a compacted, resumed or fresh session behaves the same; keep its own messages terse so a round of up to ~20 tasks fits without relying on compaction.

A permission-mode note (the command cannot set the mode): recommend launching the session in bypassPermissions — the PreToolUse hook seeded by `cairn init` (`cairn hook pre-tool-use`) still denies subagent edits to tasks.json and scopes the reviewer, and hook denies bind under bypass; `auto` mode can be tried, but its classifier may wrongly deny routine actions (git commit, bun test, cairn task); default/acceptEdits will stall an unattended round on permission prompts.
